Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

Already filed as U7.","issue":"The thesis, executive briefing and valuation rest a conclusion on \"the median twelve-month target is $338-355\" — a range presented as a median, sourced only to S142 (Tickernerd, low confidence) and S144 (TickFlow, low confidence). The conclusion drawn from it, \"there is no analyst catalyst to close the gap\", is a load-bearing part of the watchlist case and cannot bear that weight on two aggregator pages that disagree by $17.","sections":["thesis","executive_summary","funding_valuation"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Set out one dated chronology (Ninth Circuit 2025-12-11, certiorari 2026-06-30, current status) and the take-rate assumption it implies for the 2027-28 services line, and use that chronology in all three sections.","evidence_request":"The Ninth Circuit opinion of 2025-12-11 and the Supreme Court certiorari order of 2026-06-30.","issue":"The Epic link-out remedy is described three ways. Business model: the Ninth Circuit held the 27% link-out commission prohibitive and \"remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged\". ESG: the court \"limited any fee on linked transactions to Apple's costs\". ESG also records certiorari granted on 2026-06-30 with review pending, which sits awkwardly with a fee already capped at cost. The services take-rate assumption cannot be read from three incompatible statements.","sections":["business_model","esg","risk"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Use one buyback figure and one dividend per share with its declared date, and re-explain the 107% as capital returned above free cash flow funded from the cash balance, or delete it.","evidence_request":"","issue":"FY2025 buybacks are $89.3bn in strategy and $90.7bn in funding and valuation. parameters.items: [{"action":"Add each to the competitor and positioning tables with share, price and dated status, and say in one sentence why it does or does not threaten the FY2027-28 numbers; if the answer is \"not material yet\", state the evidence that says so.","evidence_request":"Android store and advertising share for Google Play and ByteDance/TikTok; China app-distribution share for Huawei AppGallery and WeChat mini-programs; EU alternative-marketplace billings for Epic, AltStore and Aptoide since 2026-10-01; Qualcomm's modem revenue guidance and any Apple C2 displacement commentary.","issue":"Five rival sets are absent or only implied. (a) Advertising: the services case cites a $1.34T pool but no ad competitor beyond Alphabet — ByteDance/TikTok and Amazon Ads, which compete for the same developer and brand budgets, are missing. (b) App distribution: Google Play is never compared as the rival store, and in China Huawei AppGallery and Tencent's WeChat mini-programs are the substitute for App Store rent. (c) The DMA's own creation — Epic Games Store, AltStore, Aptoide — appears only through Spotify. (d) The displaced modem supplier Qualcomm is a competitor the C2 claim implies. (e) Open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) are the substitute that could commoditise the rented assistant layer.","sections":["competition"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add the 2025-12-05 Google remedies ruling as the operative precedent, keep Microsoft 1998 as background, and label S145 and S147 as low and medium confidence in the table's source column.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The analog set omits the most directly comparable precedent the report itself cites: the D.C. court's 2025-12-05 remedy in US v Google, which preserved non-exclusive payments and barred exclusivity (S76, S100, S101). Microsoft 1998 rests on S147 (Wikipedia, medium) and Nokia on S145 (low confidence), so the three-analog decision rule is built on weaker sources than the precedent sitting unused in the register.","sections":["thesis","risk"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"Use the measured multiple and one source-consistent loss figure.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Small cross-section mismatches: \"Twice Apple Music's subscriber base\" against 300M and an estimated 100-108M is closer to 2.8x; Samsung's mobile division loss is KRW0.6T in competition and KRW0.8T in business model for the same Q3 2026 quarter, and the divisions are named differently (MX and Networks vs DX).","sections":["competition","business_model"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Considered and rejected as not material: Garmin (watch niche, no premium phone overlap), Sonos and Bose (premium audio, no platform rent), Visa/Mastercard (Apple Pay is a channel, not a competitor on the services margin), Sony image sensors (supplier), Microsoft Surface (no share at Apple's price points), Nvidia (supplier of compute Apple does not buy, per S118). The section's geographic coverage is otherwise sound: China, EU, US, Japan and Rest-of-Asia are all mapped with a named rival set and a regulatory status, and the status quo (longer device life) is included, which most memos omit. The gap is concentration of the services story: 40.3% of gross profit is defended in one paragraph against Spotify and Alphabet only, while the two pools that actually set App Store and search economics — alternative distribution in the EU and Chinese super-apps — are outside the table.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Replace the 9M-times-4/3 annualisation with the consensus FY2026 iPhone revenue of $252.4bn (41.2% of $613B), or label the figure \"9M annualised, seasonal distortion not adjusted\"; reconcile $149B of digital goods against S83's $1.4tn ecosystem before it is used.","evidence_request":"Counterpoint or IDC premium-segment value data, and any Apple disclosure of App Store billings, to settle the ecosystem and digital-goods figures.","issue":"Market sizes Apple's 2026 value share by annualising nine-month iPhone revenue ($196.5B x 4/3 = $262B) to get 42.7% of $613B, while the thesis and valuation use consensus FY2026 iPhone revenue of $252.4B, which gives 41.2%. The same section also cites \"an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods\" against S83, whose headline figure is a $1.4tn ecosystem — two different measures, neither reconciled.","sections":["market","thesis"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"State in the market section that Apple discloses no units, churn, upgrade or switcher rates; name the panel or tracker data that would settle each (installed-base tracker, carrier churn, regional IDC pivot) and add the four questions to the diligence list on the thesis.","evidence_request":"Counterpoint installed-base and upgrade-cycle data, or IDC's regional pivot (already requested as U3), for premium-segment unit trends and replacement rates.","issue":"The thesis is that Apple captures 36-43% of phone value on 20% of units, but there is no customer-level evidence behind it: no replacement-cycle length, no upgrade rate, no switcher in or out of iOS, no lost-deal evidence, and no statement of what would replace Apple's discontinued unit disclosure. The P/MF questions are answered only at the market level (annual September launch, consumer or carrier financing as budget owner, price elasticity inferred from IDC's pull-forward comment).","sections":["market","competition","thesis"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: The five questions, and what the report does with each. (1) Hardest thing about selling: it is answered obliquely — Apple sells through 60% indirect distribution (company overview) and the binding constraint is price, not access: a 27.6% ASP rise (S84) against a market forecast down 16.7% in units. The report does not say what the hardest part of a $1,199 sale is in a contracting market. (2) Budget owner: consumer or carrier financing plan for hardware (market), developer and subscriber for services (company overview) — correct, and the developer is the right rent-payer. (3) Sales cycle: annual September launch cycle, so the cycle is the product cadence, not a procurement cycle; the 2026 split launch (Pro and Duo in September, iPhone 18 in spring 2027) is the report's own evidence that the cadence is changing, and strategy prices it. (4) Why adoption is not faster: the report's answer is installed-base replacement plus price, and it concedes the demand test is unresolved — Siri shipped as an English beta 23 months after Apple Intelligence. (5) Lost deals: no evidence at all; the report cannot show a lost iPhone sale. That is a real limit of an issuer that stopped disclosing units in 2019, and the memo is honest about the data but not about the inference. The strongest P/MF counter-evidence the memo does marshal is China: 30% revenue growth against a market down 10%, attributed partly to pull-forward, which the market section correctly discounts.

parameters.notes: The five questions, and what the report does with each. (1) Hardest thing about selling: it is answered obliquely — Apple sells through 60% indirect distribution (company overview) and the binding constraint is price, not access: a 27.6% ASP rise (S84) against a market forecast down 16.7% in units. The report does not say what the hardest part of a $1,199 sale is in a contracting market. (2) Budget owner: consumer or carrier financing plan for hardware (market), developer and subscriber for services (company overview) — correct, and the developer is the right rent-payer. (3) Sales cycle: annual September launch cycle, so the cycle is the product cadence, not a procurement cycle; the 2026 split launch (Pro and Duo in September, iPhone 18 in spring 2027) is the report's own evidence that the cadence is changing, and strategy prices it. (4) Why adoption is not faster: the report's answer is installed-base replacement plus price, and it concedes the demand test is unresolved — Siri shipped as an English beta 23 months after Apple Intelligence. (5) Lost deals: no evidence at all; the report cannot show a lost iPhone sale. That is a real limit of an issuer that stopped disclosing units in 2019, and the memo is honest about the data but not about the inference. The strongest P/MF counter-evidence the memo does marshal is China: 30% revenue growth against a market down 10%, attributed partly to pull-forward, which the market section correctly discounts.

parameters.notes: Free cash flow and valuation arithmetic check out. FY2026 revenue $477.0bn = 9M $364.4bn + guided $112.7bn (midpoint of the 9-11% guide off $102.5bn). Rebuilding the DCF on the stated inputs (9/8/7/6/5% revenue, 33% margin, 17.5% tax, capex 0.2 points above depreciation, 4% terminal, 9.0% discount, $62.2bn net cash, 14.59bn shares) gives about $216 against the stated $212 — the base is credible and is not a bear in disguise. Normalised free cash flow also ties: $136,683M less the $14,101M other-liabilities build plus the $2,502M clean average is $125,084M; zeroing the line gives $122,582M and the best clean year $127,306M, so the $122.6-127.3bn band holds, and the deferred-consideration case ($13,531M non-current build) gives $123,152M. Stress tests: revenue 30% lower at the 43% incremental margin gives $95bn of operating income and EPS near $5.4; free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x on the $5,029.6bn value, which still covers the $82.2bn buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks plus dividends; the deferred-consideration case changes neither. The thesis survives the 30% stress on solvency and fails it on valuation, which the report already says. The two numbers that do not survive contact are the entry price's stated return and the rate sensitivity.
